title: Microsoft’s AI business is booming. A filing shows most of it is just OpenAI
excerpt: A filing shows Microsoft booked $24.1bn from OpenAI last year, about 70% of its AI sales. Even its internal Copilot now defaults to OpenAI's model.
content_html:
Microsoft’s AI business looks like a triumph. Its shares jumped after earnings last week, and the AI unit is growing fast. A new filing shows how much of that rests on a single partner.

Microsoft booked $24.1 billion in revenue from OpenAI during the year to June, Bloomberg reported. The company disclosed the figure in a filing last week. That is most of its AI business. By Bloomberg’s estimate, OpenAI is more than half of Microsoft’s actual AI sales, and probably around 70%.

It is the clearest picture yet, and the first time Microsoft has spelled the figure out. Investors have pressed the company on exactly this. One accounting researcher, Olga Usvyatsky, suggested the disclosure may be tied to OpenAI’s plans for an eventual listing.

How the 70% is built

The 70% is an estimate, not a hard number. Microsoft has only ever disclosed its total AI business twice. It did not update the figure at its latest earnings. Bloomberg assumed the unit kept growing at the 123% rate Microsoft reported in March. That would put the AI business around $34 billion for the year. Set the disclosed $24.1 billion against it, and OpenAI is roughly two thirds.

The money is not quite what it sounds. Under their agreement, OpenAI pays Microsoft for cloud computing and for the cost of building models. It also hands over a share of its revenue. Much of the $24.1 billion is OpenAI’s own compute bill, routed through Azure and booked as Microsoft income.

Against Microsoft’s total revenue, OpenAI shrinks to under 10%, closer to 7%. The concentration only jumps out when you narrow the lens to the AI unit.

Even the internal tools run on OpenAI

On the same day the number circulated, Microsoft gave a smaller sign of the same dependence. Jay Parikh runs its CoreAI engineering group. In a memo, he told staff to default to OpenAI’s flagship GPT-5.6 Sol in GitHub Copilot, CNBC reported. They should use it most of the time.

The reason he gave was money. “Shifting more workloads to OpenAI models helps us get greater value from our token investment,” Parikh wrote. Microsoft holds intellectual-property rights to OpenAI’s models through 2032. Pointing its own engineers at Sol squeezes more from that stake.

It is also part of a wider retreat from tokenmaxxing. That was the brief era when developers ran up big AI bills without watching the output. The memo was first reported by 404 Media. It lands as cheaper open-weight models, many from China, pull spending the other way.

The diversification that hasn’t landed

None of this is for lack of trying. Microsoft has built its own MAI models and offers cloud customers more than 11,000 of them. It has reached for alternatives too, including a $5 billion bet on Anthropic. GitHub Copilot alone, now past 50 million users, serves models from Anthropic, Google, Moonshot, xAI, and Microsoft itself.

And yet the filing says roughly 70% of the AI revenue still traces to OpenAI. The effort to spread the risk has not moved the number that matters.

Engine or exposure

Whether that reads as strength or fragility depends on what the money is. KeyBanc analyst Jackson Ader wants to know where it comes from. Is it services sold to OpenAI, or the benefit of Microsoft’s own investment? “The more of that revenue comes from services to OpenAI,” he said, “the more favorably I’m going to look at it.”

The bears are blunter. The writer Ed Zitron notes Microsoft has spent more than $260 billion on capital projects since 2022. He argues much of its AI revenue is OpenAI’s compute bill dressed as growth. If OpenAI stumbles, Microsoft is left with the sunk cost and the empty data centres.

There is no sign of a stumble. The AI unit is still growing fast, which is why the stock climbed. But the filing settles a long argument with an uncomfortable answer. After years of work and hundreds of billions in spending to become more than OpenAI’s landlord, Microsoft, for now, mostly is one.

content_html_zh:
微软的人工智能业务看起来取得了胜利。 上周公布财报后，该公司股价大幅上涨，人工智能部门正在快速增长。 一份新的文件显示了其中有多少取决于单一合作伙伴。

据彭博社报道，截至 6 月份的一年中，微软从 OpenAI 获得了 241 亿美元的收入。 该公司在上周的一份文件中披露了这一数字。 这是其大部分人工智能业务。 据彭博社估计，OpenAI 占微软实际 AI 销售额的一半以上，可能在 70% 左右。

这是迄今为止最清晰的图片，也是微软第一次阐明这个数字。 投资者正是在这一点上向该公司施压。 一位会计研究员 Olga Usvyatsky 表示，此次披露可能与 OpenAI 的最终上市计划有关。

70%是如何构建的

70% 是一个估计值，而不是一个硬性数字。 微软仅两次披露其人工智能业务总量。 它没有更新最新财报中的数字。 彭博社预计该部门将继续以微软 3 月份报告的 123% 的速度增长。 这将使今年的人工智能业务收入约为 340 亿美元。 如果将披露的 241 亿美元与它相比，OpenAI 大约是三分之二。

钱并不像听起来那样。 根据他们的协议，OpenAI 向微软支付云计算和构建模型的费用。 它还上交了一部分收入。 这 241 亿美元中的大部分是 OpenAI 自己的计算账单，通过 Azure 传输并记为微软收入。

相对于微软的总收入，OpenAI 缩减至 10% 以下，接近 7%。 只有当你将镜头缩小到人工智能单元时，注意力才会跳出来。

甚至内部工具也运行在 OpenAI 上

在该数字流传的同一天，微软也给出了同样依赖的较小信号。 Jay Parikh 负责管理 CoreAI 工程团队。 据 CNBC 报道，他在一份备忘录中告诉员工在 GitHub Copilot 中默认使用 OpenAI 的旗舰产品 GPT-5.6 Sol。 他们应该大部分时间都使用它。

他给出的理由是钱。 “将更多工作负载转移到 OpenAI 模型有助于我们从代币投资中获得更大价值，”Parikh 写道。 到 2032 年，微软将拥有 OpenAI 模型的知识产权。 将自己的工程师指向 Sol 可以从这笔股份中榨取更多利益。

这也是更广泛地退出代币最大化的一部分。 那是一个短暂的时代，开发人员在不关注输出的情况下就收取了大量的人工智能费用。 该备忘录最先由 404 Media 报道。 它以更便宜的开放式重量模型登陆，其中许多来自中国，以另一种方式拉动支出。

尚未落地的多元化

这一切都不是因为缺乏尝试。 Microsoft 已经构建了自己的 MAI 模型，并向云客户提供了超过 11,000 个模型。 它还寻求替代方案，包括对 Anthropic 下注 50 亿美元。 仅 GitHub Copilot 现已拥有超过 5000 万用户，为 Anthropic、Google、Moonshot、xAI 和 Microsoft 本身的模型提供服务。

然而文件称，大约 70% 的人工智能收入仍然来自 OpenAI。 分散风险的努力并没有改变重要的数字。

引擎或暴露

这到底是强大还是脆弱取决于金钱的多少。 KeyBanc 分析师 Jackson Ader 想知道它来自哪里。 是卖给OpenAI的服务，还是微软自己投资的收益？ “来自 OpenAI 服务的收入越多，”他说，“我就越看好它。”

熊则比较迟钝。 作者 Ed Zitron 指出，自 2022 年以来，微软在资本项目上的支出已超过 2600 亿美元。 他认为，其人工智能收入的大部分来自 OpenAI 伪装成增长的计算费用。 如果 OpenAI 失败，微软将面临沉没成本和空置的数据中心。

没有任何绊倒的迹象。 人工智能部门仍在快速增长，这就是该股上涨的原因。 但该文件以一个令人不安的答案解决了长期争论。 经过多年的努力和数千亿美元的支出，微软已经超越了 OpenAI 的领主，目前基本上已经是其中之一了。
